industry-lifecycle.prompt: Order the pipeline as it actually runs in an organisation.
industry-lifecycle.steps[0].label: Understand the Business Problem and Stakeholders
industry-lifecycle.steps[0].detail: Who is affected, who decides, and what a good outcome is for them. Skipping this is how technically sound models get built for the wrong problem.
industry-lifecycle.steps[1].label: Define the ML Task, Constraints, and Success Metrics
industry-lifecycle.steps[1].detail: Fix the target, the latency and cost budget, and the metric before any data is touched, so success cannot be redefined after the fact.
industry-lifecycle.steps[2].label: Source Data and Establish Governance
industry-lifecycle.steps[2].detail: Establish lawful basis, licence, consent and retention up front. Data acquired without them is a liability that no later step removes.
industry-lifecycle.steps[3].label: Ingest, Catalogue, and Version Data
industry-lifecycle.steps[3].detail: Land the data with a catalogue entry and a version. Without versioning no result is reproducible and no regression is explainable.
industry-lifecycle.steps[4].label: Explore Data and Validate Quality
industry-lifecycle.steps[4].detail: Profile distributions, nulls, duplicates and outliers before modelling, because every one of them shows up later as unexplained error.
industry-lifecycle.steps[5].label: Clean, Transform, and Label Data
industry-lifecycle.steps[5].detail: Repair what can be repaired and label what needs labels, with the labelling guidance itself treated as a versioned artefact.
industry-lifecycle.steps[6].label: Engineer and Select Features
industry-lifecycle.steps[6].detail: Build the representations the model will use, and drop the ones that leak the target or will not exist at inference time.
industry-lifecycle.steps[7].label: Create Training, Validation, and Test Splits
industry-lifecycle.steps[7].detail: Split before fitting anything, respecting time and group boundaries. A split made after preprocessing has already leaked.
industry-lifecycle.steps[8].label: Build a Reproducible Baseline
industry-lifecycle.steps[8].detail: A simple model that runs end to end. It sets the bar every later candidate must clear and proves the pipeline works.
industry-lifecycle.steps[9].label: Train Candidate Models and Track Experiments
industry-lifecycle.steps[9].detail: Fit alternatives with their configuration, data version and results recorded, so the winner can be rebuilt months later.
industry-lifecycle.steps[10].label: Tune Hyperparameters with Validation Data
industry-lifecycle.steps[10].detail: Search settings against validation data only. Tuning against test data turns the final number into self-assessment.
industry-lifecycle.steps[11].label: Evaluate Quality, Robustness, Fairness, and Security
industry-lifecycle.steps[11].detail: Test held-out quality, behaviour under perturbation, performance by subgroup, and adversarial exposure. One aggregate accuracy number hides all three of the others.
industry-lifecycle.steps[12].label: Document, Approve, Package, and Register the Model
industry-lifecycle.steps[12].detail: Record intended use, limits and evaluation results, get the accountable approval, and register the artefact. This is what makes deployment reviewable.
industry-lifecycle.steps[13].label: Deploy Gradually with Automated Tests and Rollback
industry-lifecycle.steps[13].detail: Shadow, canary or staged rollout with a tested path back. Gradual exposure is what makes a bad release survivable.
industry-lifecycle.steps[14].label: Monitor Data, Model, System, and Business Performance
industry-lifecycle.steps[14].detail: Watch all four layers. Inputs drift, quality decays, infrastructure fails and business value erodes — and they are not the same signal.
industry-lifecycle.steps[15].label: Collect Feedback, Retrain, Revalidate, or Retire
industry-lifecycle.steps[15].detail: Feed production reality back in, and decide deliberately between retraining, revalidating and retirement. A model with no retirement criterion never gets retired.
